about.title: Calexico Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Calexico sits along busy border-adjacent corridors, and traffic on Rt 111, Rt 98, Cole Road, and Cesar Chavez sees steady movement throughout the week, with reported collisions tending to cluster on Tuesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. Whether you were stopped at a light, merging near one of these roads, or driving through a residential stretch, a sudden collision can leave you dealing with medical bills, missed work, and an insurance adjuster who's already calling. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects injured Calexico residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate what happened and explain your options under California law. Every case is different, and time matters: evidence fades, memories change, and insurers move quickly to close files in their favor. Getting matched with someone who understands the local roads and how these claims typically unfold can make the process less overwhelming while you focus on recovering.

whyChoose.title: Why Act Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: California's Filing Deadline Is Firm
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Missing it usually means losing the right to recover anything.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you're partly at fault, but your share of fault reduces what you can recover. An early recorded statement to the other driver's insurer can be used to inflate your share of blame before you've even spoken with an attorney.

items.title: Evidence on Roads Like Rt 111 or Cole Road Disappears Fast
items.desc: Skid marks fade, surveillance footage gets overwritten, and witnesses move on. Preserving photos, dashcam footage, and contact information early gives an attorney more to work with when building your case.

items.question: Do I have to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: No, you're not required to give a recorded statement to the other party's insurer, and it's generally better not to before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can shift blame onto you. An independent attorney can advise you on what to say and when.

items.question: How long do I have to file a car accident claim in Calexico?
items.answer: California generally gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If your accident involved a government-owned vehicle or a road maintained by a public agency, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking your specific situation quickly.

items.question: What if my accident happened on Rt 111 or another busy Calexico corridor?
items.answer: Corridors like Rt 111, Rt 98, Cole Road, and Cesar Chavez see regular traffic flow, and where an accident occurred can affect who's responsible and what evidence is available. An attorney familiar with how these claims are handled locally can help sort out the details specific to your crash.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything for connecting me with an attorney?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is a free service — there's no cost to you for the connection itself. Attorneys in the network typically work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if you recover compensation.
